title: Tabular, summary, matrix, and joined reports
objectives: Name the four report formats and what each grouping pattern is for.
Choose tabular, summary, matrix, or joined from a business question—not from habit.
Explain that joined reports combine multiple report types in blocks, with a principal type.
Cite display and joined-report limits from Salesforce Help rather than inventing numbers.
diagnostic_question: A VP wants Opportunities grouped by Stage down the side and by Close Month across the top, plus a side-by-side Cases block from a different report type. Which formats do you use, and what do you refuse to fake with a tabular list?
definition: A Salesforce report uses one of four formats: tabular (no groupings), summary (grouped by rows), matrix (grouped by rows and columns), or joined (multiple report types in blocks). Help tells you to pick a format complex enough to capture the data but simple enough to communicate it. ([Build a Report](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_builder_editing.htm); [Joined reports](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.knowledge_feedback_create_report.htm))
why_it_matters: Format is the interview tell after report type. Tabular cannot answer a two-axis question. Matrix is not a joined report. Joined blocks still each need a report type. Limits such as 2,000 displayed rows and five joined blocks are Help facts, not folklore.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of four newspaper layouts. Tabular is the classifieds: a flat list. Summary is the sports section grouped by team down the page. Matrix is the box-score grid: teams down, weeks across. Joined is the Sunday paper: several sections (report types) bound together, each with its own columns. You pick the layout after you pick which menu (report type) feeds the section.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce Help lists tabular, summary, matrix, or joined as the formats a report can use. Group data in columns or rows in summary, matrix, and joined reports. Tabular has no groupings. ([Build a Report in Salesforce Classic](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_builder_editing.htm))

A joined report contains data from reports of different types, including standard and custom report types, so you can present different kinds of information in one report. The first type you pick becomes the principal report type; additional types are added as blocks. ([Create a Joined Report for Knowledge Feedback](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.knowledge_feedback_create_report.htm))

Reports display a maximum of 2,000 rows. Printable view for tabular and summary can show more; joined printable view shows a maximum of 20,000 rows and is Classic-only. Matrix reports that return more than 2,000 rows do not show details. Joined reports allow up to 5 blocks and 100 columns per block. ([Reports and Dashboards Limits and Allocations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm))
On mobile, reports that have groupings are converted to tabular. Format is report metadata; the rows are still business data queried through the report type and sharing.

Summary formulas and charts often need groupings; that is why summary or matrix is the usual dashboard source pattern. Exact dashboard-source rules for tabular row limits: Needs verification in current dashboard Help before quoting a UI click path.

mental_model.analogy: Four newspaper layouts sharing the same wire copy (report type): classifieds, grouped sports section, box-score grid, and a Sunday multi-section paper.
useful_mapping: summary → section grouped by a headline down the page
matrix → box score with categories on two axes
joined → Sunday paper with multiple sections (report types)
principal report type → the section you started the joined paper with
block → one section with its own columns
2,000-row display cap → the newsstand copy that truncates a long list
report format metadata → the layout template, not the events being reported
where_it_breaks: Newspapers do not inner-join related objects; the report type still does (ANA-001).
Mobile converts grouped reports to tabular—paper does not change in your pocket that way.
Joined printable-view row caps differ from on-screen 2,000 rows.
The analogy does not encode dashboard running user (ANA-004).

claims.claim: A report can use the tabular, summary, matrix, or joined format. Summary, matrix, and joined can group data; tabular has no groupings.
claims.validation: Report Formats and Group Your Report Data sections in the Classic builder Help article.

claims.claim: A joined report combines different report types in one report. The first type selected is the principal report type; more types are added as blocks.
claims.validation: Create a Joined Report for Knowledge Feedback.

claims.claim: Reports display a maximum of 2,000 rows. Joined reports allow up to 5 blocks and 100 columns per block. Matrix reports over 2,000 rows do not show details. Grouped reports become tabular in the Salesforce mobile app.
claims.validation: Reports and Dashboards Limits and Allocations.

changed_in_release: Lightning report builder format switching UI should be rechecked each release. Joined-report limits in the allocations article are the cited numbers for Summer '26 verification.
unresolved_uncertainty: Whether a given tabular report can feed a Lightning dashboard component without a row limit: confirm in current dashboard Help before stating a hard rule.
Cross-block summary formula limits are listed in Help (10 cross-block formulas; 10 custom summary formulas per joined block; 50 total)—cite the limits article rather than memory in interviews.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Four formats: tabular is a list, summary groups rows, matrix groups rows and columns, joined stitches multiple report types into blocks. Pick format after report type. On screen you still cap at about 2,000 rows.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the question shape. A mailing-style list is tabular. Pipeline by owner is summary. Stage by month is matrix. Cases beside Opportunities from different types is joined: first type is principal, then Add Block. I never call matrix a joined report. I mention Help limits: five blocks, 100 columns per block, matrix hiding details past 2,000 rows, mobile flattening groupings to tabular. Format is metadata; rows remain data.

terminology.plain: A flat list of rows with no groupings.
terminology.precise: The format with no row or column groupings. Help preview shows up to 50 rows for tabular.
terminology.example: A LAB_Contact phone list with no grouping.
terminology.non_example: Opportunities grouped by Stage (that is summary).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Export/printable view: a way to see more rows, not a fifth format.
terminology.boundary: Dashboard-source eligibility for tabular: Needs verification in current dashboard Help.

terminology.plain: A report grouped by one or more fields down the page, with subtotals.
terminology.precise: Grouped by rows. Preview shows a maximum of 20 rows in the builder for summary reports grouped by rows.
terminology.example: Opportunities grouped by Owner, then by Stage.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Summary formula (ANA-003): a calculation on groups, not the format name.
terminology.boundary: Mobile converts grouped reports to tabular.

terminology.plain: A grid grouped both down and across.
terminology.precise: Grouped by rows and by columns. If it returns more than 2,000 rows, details do not show.
terminology.example: Opportunity Amount by Stage (rows) and Close Month (columns).
terminology.non_example: Two report types in separate blocks (joined).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Joined report: multiple types, not two grouping axes on one type.
terminology.boundary: Matrix summarized-value caps with summary formulas are in the limits article.

terminology.plain: One report that shows blocks from different report types.
terminology.precise: Combines standard and custom report types. First type is principal; add blocks for more. Up to 5 blocks, 100 columns each.
terminology.example: Knowledge Article Feedback block plus Survey Responses block.
terminology.non_example: A custom report type that relates Account to Contact (still one type).
terminology.boundary: Row counts and summaries can be inaccurate when a joined report exceeds 2,000 rows and one block dominates.

terminology.plain: The first report type you pick when starting a joined report.
terminology.precise: Help: the report type you select becomes the joined report's principal report type.
terminology.example: Starting from Knowledge Article Feedback, then adding Survey Responses as a block.
terminology.non_example: The running user on a dashboard.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Primary object on a custom report type.
terminology.boundary: How Lightning labels 'principal' in the UI: confirm in-org.

terminology.plain: One pane inside a joined report, tied to one report type.
terminology.precise: Each block can have up to 100 columns. A joined report can have up to 5 blocks.
terminology.non_example: A dashboard widget is not a joined-report block.
terminology.boundary: Cross-block formulas are a later filter/formula skill (ANA-003) with their own caps.

terminology.plain: Bucketing rows under a field so subtotals make sense.
terminology.precise: Available in summary, matrix, and joined reports. Nested groupings are allowed.
terminology.example: Group by Close Date, then by Type.
terminology.non_example: A filter is not a grouping.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Bucket field (ANA-003): a report-local category column.
terminology.boundary: Too many groups hit chart and dashboard grouping caps (ANA-005).

terminology.plain: The on-screen report stops at 2,000 rows.
terminology.precise: Help: reports display a maximum of 2,000 rows. Export or Classic printable view for more; joined printable view max 20,000 rows.
terminology.example: A tabular export when the on-screen list is truncated.
terminology.non_example: Custom report type allocation (that is a count of types, not rows).
terminology.boundary: Performance timeouts (10 minutes default) are a separate limit.

when_to_use: When you must pick tabular, summary, matrix, or joined from a stakeholder's question shape.
When two different report types must appear in one joined report with a principal type and extra blocks.
When a two-axis grid (for example Stage by month) needs a matrix report rather than a summary list.
When you need to cite the 2,000-row display cap or the five-block joined limit from Help.
when_not_to_use: Do not use joined reports to replace a custom report type when the real gap is a missing related object (ANA-001).
Do not use matrix format when a summary grouping plus a chart would communicate the same single-axis story.
Do not promise a tabular report will show every row on screen past the 2,000-row display limit.
Do not treat report format as a substitute for CRM Analytics datasets or Tableau workbooks (ANA-006).

decision_table.signal: Need a simple list of records with no subtotals by category.
decision_table.not: Matrix or joined 'to look more official.'
decision_table.why: Tabular is the no-grouping format; extra axes add noise.

decision_table.signal: Need subtotals grouped down the page by Owner or Stage.
decision_table.not: Tabular plus a spreadsheet pivot after every run.
decision_table.why: Summary is the grouped-by-rows format in Help.

decision_table.signal: Need a grid with one field down and another across, such as Stage by month.
decision_table.choose: Matrix report grouped by rows and columns.
decision_table.not: A joined report with two copies of the same type.
decision_table.why: Matrix is two axes on one report type; joined is multiple types.

decision_table.signal: Need Opportunities and Cases from different report types in one report.
decision_table.choose: Joined report: principal type plus additional blocks.
decision_table.not: A custom report type that pretends unrelated objects are a parent-child chain.
decision_table.why: Help defines joined reports as combining different report types.

decision_table.signal: The on-screen report stops at 2,000 rows or matrix details will not show.
decision_table.choose: Filter the report or export / Classic printable view per Help.
decision_table.not: Switching to joined format hoping the cap disappears.
decision_table.why: Joined reports still have row-accuracy warnings past 2,000 rows.

limitations: Does not replace custom report type design (ANA-001).
Does not teach filters, cross filters, or formulas (ANA-003).
Mobile flattens grouped reports to tabular.
Joined printable view is Classic-only per the limits article.
security_notes: Each joined block still respects the running user's access to that report type's objects.
Do not export real customer rows into personal email as a workaround for the 2,000-row cap without a data policy.
common_mistakes: Calling a matrix report a joined report.
Using joined format because a field is missing from the type (fix the type).
Forgetting mobile users will see groupings as tabular.

interview_questions.question: Explain tabular, summary, matrix, and joined reports.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Tabular is a list with no groupings. Summary groups rows. Matrix groups rows and columns. Joined puts multiple report types in blocks, starting with a principal type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick format after report type. Phone lists are tabular. Pipeline by owner is summary. Stage by month is matrix. Opportunities beside Cases from different types is joined: first type principal, then Add Block, max five blocks and 100 columns each. I cite the 2,000-row on-screen cap so nobody thinks the UI is a complete extract. Format is metadata; rows are data.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Matrix_StageMonth versus LAB_Joined_OppCase as two different answers to two different questions.
weak_answer_warnings: Treating matrix and joined as synonyms

interview_questions.question: When is a joined report the right tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When you must show different report types together, including standard and custom types, as blocks in one report—not when you merely need two grouping axes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's Knowledge example starts from one type, applies joined format, and adds Survey Responses as a second block. That is the pattern: principal type plus Add Block. If the real problem is a missing child object on one type, I go back to a custom report type. If the real problem is Stage by Month, I use matrix. I stay inside five blocks and watch the 2,000-row accuracy warning.
interview_questions.example: Knowledge Article Feedback plus Survey Responses in one joined report.
tradeoffs: Joined complexity vs two separate reports on a dashboard
follow_ups: What is a principal report type?

interview_questions.question: A VP wants a spreadsheet-style grid of Stage versus Close Month. What do you build?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A matrix report grouped by Stage and Close Month on the Opportunities report type—not a joined report and not a tabular dump.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Two axes on one type is matrix. I confirm Close Date is groupable and that filters keep the grid under painful grouping counts. If they also want Cases in the same grid, that is a different question: either a dashboard with two components or a joined report with two blocks, which still will not magically cross-tab Cases against Opportunity Stage. I warn that past 2,000 rows matrix hides details.
interview_questions.example: LAB Opportunities matrix: Stage rows, calendar month columns, Amount summarized.
tradeoffs: Matrix density vs a summary plus chart
follow_ups: What if they insist on seeing every Opportunity line in the grid?
Would a dashboard gauge replace this?
weak_answer_warnings: Building joined with two Opportunity types

interview_questions.question: Leadership wants 'one report to rule Opportunities and unrelated custom objects with no lookup.' How do you answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Joined reports still need real report types per block. They do not invent a relationship. If there is no type, we create CRTs or we use a dashboard with multiple reports—or a later analytics product.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate three tools. Custom report type: parent-child or lookup graph. Joined: multiple types side by side. Dashboard: multiple widgets. If objects are truly unrelated, a fake CRT inner join is dishonest. I may offer a joined report with two honest blocks, or two reports on one dashboard. I will not promise a matrix of unrelated objects. CRM Analytics might be in scope later (ANA-006), but not as a silent substitute in this answer.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Event__c with no lookup to Opportunity: two blocks or two widgets, not one invented CRT.
follow_ups: When would you escalate to CRM Analytics?

interview_questions.question: Users say the matrix report 'lost its rows' when they click Show Details.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If a matrix report returns more than 2,000 rows, Help says details do not show. Filter or use Details Only export rather than assuming the format broke.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check the result size first. The limits article is explicit: Show Details does nothing over 2,000 rows; export Details Only. I also check they are not on mobile, where groupings flatten to tabular. I do not rebuild as joined hoping the cap vanishes—joined reports have their own accuracy warning past 2,000 rows. I then add filters or split by date so the grid is usable.
interview_questions.example: Unfiltered all-time Opportunities matrix; Show Details inert until Close Date this quarter is applied.
tradeoffs: Split reports vs one giant matrix
weak_answer_warnings: Switching to joined as a magic fix

interview_questions.question: A joined report's totals look wrong on a huge org. What does Help warn?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Row counts and summaries can be inaccurate in a joined report with more than 2,000 rows when one block takes most of the rows.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat joined totals as untrusted once we are past the display cap with an unbalanced block. I filter each block, split into two reports, or export. I also check we have not exceeded 5 blocks or 100 columns. I explain that printable view in Classic can show up to 20,000 rows for joined, which is still not 'unlimited.' I do not 'fix' this with a summary formula that reads the broken totals.
interview_questions.example: Opportunities block returns 1,900 rows and Cases 200; totals look plausible until both grow and one dominates.
follow_ups: Would a dashboard metric be safer?
weak_answer_warnings: Guaranteeing joined totals at any scale

interview_questions.question: How do you choose format without defaulting to matrix for every executive?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I map question shape: no groups tabular, one axis summary, two axes matrix, multiple types joined. Executives often want a dashboard, not a denser report format.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Format is not seniority. A CRO phone list is still tabular. A CRO pipeline by region is summary. A CRO Stage-by-month grid is matrix. A CRO 'Opportunities and Cases on one page' may be a dashboard of two summary reports rather than a joined report they cannot read on a phone. Mobile flattens groupings to tabular, so I ask where they will open it. I keep report type decisions in ANA-001 and filters in ANA-003.
interview_questions.example: VP asked for 'a matrix of everything'; you delivered a summary plus a dashboard chart instead, and documented why.
tradeoffs: Mobile tabular flattening vs desktop matrix
follow_ups: When is joined better than a dashboard?
Preview row limits in the builder?

interview_questions.question: Teach the four formats with a newspaper analogy and then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Tabular is classifieds, summary is a grouped sports section, matrix is a box-score grid, joined is the Sunday multi-section paper. The analogy breaks on mobile flattening and the 2,000-row cap.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep report type as the wire service feeding every layout. Joined sections are different report types, not two axes. I add Help numbers: five blocks, 100 columns, matrix details hidden past 2,000 rows. I say newspapers do not enforce FLS. I refuse a library or labeled-drawer story. I finish by asking the interviewer which layout their last VP actually needed.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard the four layouts, then write the 2,000-row and 5-block limits underneath.
tradeoffs: One analogy vs mixing dashboards in too early
follow_ups: Where does the newspaper analogy break?
